findings.message: Bug LP: #2155998 is not targeted at os-prober and resolute

blockers.summary: The Ubuntu Foundations reviewer (juliank) says the problem has not been reproduced or understood from the boot side and the patch may not make sense, and the original hanging-mount bug was meanwhile fixed differently with mount namespaces. The fix's rationale needs to be re-validated before it can be released.

The 'Where problems could occur' section is factually wrong. os-prober is not disabled by default, because it is automatically enabled when other OSes are detected at install time. The section also does not analyse what the fuseblk fallback path actually does before removing it, so the real regression potential is undetermined.

The test plan does not describe verifying the fix, such as running update-grub with the patched package and confirming the snapshot entry is gone. It also does not check that other filesystems that previously fell back to fuseblk (for example NTFS or other FUSE-detected types) are still probed. The 'Post the fix' statement is only an assertion.

The bug text says the fix should later be backported to Noble and Jammy, and that the earlier hanging-mount fix is absent there. The target series for this SRU is unclear, and the interaction with the mount-namespace approach is unaddressed.

He says nullboot SRUs go through a 0.6.1 release (possibly a 0.5.4 for older series) and are not uploaded one patch at a time by non-boot people, so the proposed debdiffs may be rejected unless coordinated with him.

The reviewer asked whether nullboot's special SRU handling should be documented in the package-specific SRU reference page. Nobody has answered or followed up.

The test plan is a flaky-reproduction loop that only runs on an Azure CVM. It has no expected pass/fail criteria for the fixed package and no check for regressions on boot or resealing, which matters for a boot-related package. Maintainers said testing is needed, especially because 0.6.0 includes large secboot library changes. The risk assessment says it is low but does not cover how the patch applies to older versions such as jammy and noble.
